findings.title: Hardcoded secret credential exposed in source
findings.body: The constant `PARTNER_TOKEN` on line 3 contains a hardcoded secret credential (`FAKE_TEST_CREDENTIAL_DO_NOT_USE`). This violates the OWASP Top 10 (CWE-798) and risks accidental exposure in logs, version control, or runtime memory. Secrets must be injected via environment variables or a secure vault.

findings.title: Token comparison uses direct equality without constant-time comparison
findings.body: The function `can_read_private_records` compares the input token directly with `PARTNER_TOKEN` using `==` on line 6. This exposes the secret to timing attacks. Use a constant-time comparison (e.g., `secrets.compare_digest`) to mitigate timing side-channel leaks.

summary.problem: The new authorization module hardcodes a secret credential and uses an unsafe comparison, introducing critical security risks.
summary.done_well: The function signature and logic are minimal and focused on a single responsibility.
